wrong key
A key will not open the door you expected.

The key turned but the door didn't open. I leaned on it. Something heavy was behind it, not a chain because there wasn't any give. I could get a finger round the edge at the top. Light on inside. I called through the letterbox and heard someone moving away. Then my phone rang. It was the landlord asking why I was at the old address. He'd changed the viewing. The person inside started pushing the door back and my key snapped in the lock.
Measurements
A room is bigger than the building should allow.

From the kitchen wall to the back fence was nine metres. The cellar should have been four metres wide. It was eleven. I checked with the laser measure, then with the tape because the laser can bounce off glass and there was a shiny patch on the far wall. Eleven either way. That meant we were under next door's garden. Possibly under next door. I'd only gone down to look at the damp. Now I was sketching floor plans on the back of an invoice while the estate agnet stood at the top of the stairs saying old houses are full of surprises. There was a small door behind a shelving unit. I moved the shelves. She stopped talking. I asked if she had the key and she said the surveyor hadn't mentioned a door.
Latch
Someone forgets to lock up.
I locked the workshop then pulled the handle to check. Came off in my hand. The door stayed shut. I stood there holding it, thinking I should have stopped after the first part.
red boots
A child refuses to go home.

She sat down in the puddle. Just sat. We had been arguing about going home for so long that I didn't understand what she was doing until the water came over her waist. She looked surprised too. Her red boots floated up in front of her. I pulled her out by the armpits and she began screaming, not because she was wet but because I'd taken her out. A man with a little white dog watched the whole thing. He said they grow up so fast. I nearly threw a boot at him. On the way home she fell asleep against my neck, wet all through her clothes. I could feel the cold through my coat. Her hand was still holding a leaf she'd refused to drop.
the bell
An old sound returns.

The bell sounded wrong because it was the same. Everything else at the school was new: fence, windows, a whole extra building where the sandpit had been. But that awful metallic rattle still made my stomach do the thing. I was there for my niece's concert. Her teacher told us to line up outside the hall and I actually stood straighter. I'm thirty. I pay bills. A woman in a cardigan can still make me feel like I'm about to lose break time. Inside, someone had polished the floor and it smelled exactly like wet pencil shavings. My niece waved so hard her cardboard crown slipped. I waved back with both hands, which embarrassed my sister.
Rain
Describe waiting indoors.

waiting for it to stop raining but it keeps starting harder just when it sounds like it might stop. the kitchen window is fogged at the bottom. drew a dog in it. looks like a chair. that's all i've got today.
the long way
A familiar shortcut has changed.

We couldn't get through the alley because somebody had built a gate. My cousin said it had always been there. It hadn't. We'd ridden scooters through that alley every summer. I showed her the scratch on the wall where I'd lost a handlebar, but the wall had been painted and the scratch was gone. She didn't remember the scooters either. She remembered bikes. I got stupidly upset upset. It wasn't even about the gate by then. We walked round the block in silence and found the corner shop was now a place selling expensive soap. She bought some. I waited outside trying to remember whether my scooter had been red or yellow, which made the whole argument feel worse.
Biscuit policy
A small office dispute grows.

Someone put a spreadhseet beside the biscuit tin. A SPREADSHEET. Names, dates, number consumed. I ate a biscuit while reading it and immediately felt like a criminal. Was I supposed to log the broken half? Were crumbs taxable? I wrote 'Lee, today, several' and went back to my desk. At eleven Carol came round with the sheet asking who had written several. My name was next to it Carol. We have reached the point where literacy is optional but biscuit accountability is mandatory. Anyway she says it's for stock control and I said then why is there a column called habitual. She said that was unfortunate wording. I have been labelled a habitual biscuit user and HR won't answer my email.
mug
Something small goes missing.

My mug is gone and everyone is being NORMAL about it. That's the worst bit. They've all still got drinks. Nobody has paused operations. Mine is the blue one with no handle, which I know sounds like a bowl but it is a mug with history. I found it in the meeting room holding pens. Asked whose idea that was. Nobody knew. Took the pens out, washed it, made tea, sat down. It leaked. Someone had put pens in it BECAUSE it leaked. I had forgotten that. Now there's tea in my keyboard and I have to go round explaining why I accused everybody of theft. Might just go home.
Untitled Sprint
Someone saves the best bit for later.

Saved the crispy bit of lasagne till last and then sneezed on it. Proper sneeze, no time to turn away. It's my own sneeze so technically what's the problem. I eat things that have been in my own mouth all the time. That's chewing. But now I've thought about chewing too much and can't eat anything. The lasagne is geting cold. I was looking forward to that bit all afternoon. This is a bad story. It's also my lunch.
lunch
An interruption at lunchtime.

Phone rang while I was eating. I answered with a mouth full of rice and said 'hello speaking' which isn't anything. They asked for someone called Martin. I said yes. Why did I say yes. Now I'm Martin and they've got a quote for my roof.
leaving card
You cannot think what to write.

What do you write in a leaving card for a man whose name you learned from the leaving card. 'All the best' is taken four times. 'Good luck' three. Someone wrote 'onwards and upwards' which makes it sound like he's died climbing stairs. I started 'It's been a pleasure' and then realised I couldn't finish that honestly. It's been a pleasure sharing a printer with you Nigel. Except he always left the tray empty. Now I'm holding up the whole card chain and Carol is hovering. Wrote 'Enjoy the next chapter!' I don't know if he's got another job. Could be retiring. Could be going to prison. Chapters covers most things.
borrowed magic
A spell has a small side effect.

The spell made everyone speak kindly for one day. Grandmother said that was a lovely idea right before it took effect, which should have warned us. By lunch she was telling the postman he had a beautiful large head. Mum complimented the neighbour's remarkably persistent dog. Nobody could ask anyone to stop doing anything. I tried telling my brother to stop eating the spell ingredients and called him a resourceful little treasure. He ate the whole jar. Now we don't know how to undo it.
winter apples
A tree gives something other than fruit.

The apple tree gave gloves that winter. Mostly left ones. We hung them in pairs where we could and gave the odd ones to people who'd lost a hand, but there were only two such people in the village and they didn't need forty gloves each. Father wanted to chop the tree down. Mother said wait till spring.

In March it grew sleeves. In April a whole coat. By June there was a man hanging upside down from the highest branch, asleep, with his shoes tied together. He wasn't a prince. We checked. He was a tailor from the next valley and he was very cross about the way we had pruned his fingers.
the wish
A wish brings someone back differently.

I wished that my brother would come back. The woman at the well asked which brother, and I said I only had one. She asked if I was certain. I was annoyed because this was supposed to be the sad part and she was making it complicated. Yes, I said. Then there were footsteps behind me. My brother was there, but small, the size he'd been before he went away. He had mud on his knees and wanted to know where his wooden horse was. I didn't know how to explain that I'd burned it after the letter came. The woman at the well had gone. He took my hand and asked why I was old. I started walking him home.
the pump
Someone tries to repair an old bicycle.

The pump was fine. I blamed the pump for about half an hour before realising the the valve had come loose. Took the wheel off and lost one of the nuts in the gravel. Then found a different nut which looked close enough but wasn't. I used to do this stuff without thinking. Now I have to watch a video to remember which way the tyre goes. My son kept asking if we were still going out. I said yes too many times. By the time I got it fixed he'd taken his bike down the road with his mates. I went round the block on my own. Brakes rubbed all the way. Need to sort those next.
Saturday
A team has too few players.

Seven of us turned up. You need eleven, obviously, but the other lot only had nine so we agreed on a smaller pitch. Then Dave brought his brother. Then their keeper's cousin arrived. We spent longer counting people than playing. I went in goal because my knee was bad and immediately had to dive on it. Nobody scored for twenty minutes. It wasn't good defending, just terrible shooting.

At half time we stood round someone's boot drinking orange squash from cups left over from a birthday party. Mine had a unicorn on it. Dave asked if I fancied the league again next year. I said probably. Knee says no but I always say probably.
Bench
An unfinished repair.
Sanded half the bench then it rained. Brought it inside. Too wide for the door. Left it on its side under a bin bag. This was meant to be the easy job this weekend.
last lap
Someone keeps going after the race ends.

I thought there was another lap. That's it, that's the story. Everyone stopped and I kept going because I'd lost count around lap four when my shoelace came undone. A woman shouted something but I thought she was encouraging me. So I ran a whole extra lap and came back to find them packing the clock away. My wife had my medal in her bag. She'd collected it because she thought I'd gone to the toilet. I was angry for about ten minutes, then tired, then hungry. We went for chips. I still put the distance in my running app because I had run it, regardless of whether anybody was counting.
seat
You want to sit beside someone.

theres a seat next to her but her bag is on it so maybe she doesnt want anyone there. i could ask. i ask people things all day why is this diffrent. because if she says no i'll have to sit somewhere else and she'll know i tried. which is not actually a disaster. okay i'm going to ask. she looked up and moved the bag before i said anything and now i've forgot how to say thanks
the message
A difficult message remains unsent.

i wrote hey about six times. hey sounds too casual but hello sounds like i'm selling something. i want to ask if she's angry with me but if she isn't then she might become angry because i keep asking. last time she said she was tired. people can be tired. i am tired right now from thinking about a text nobody's even received. recieved. i never spell that right. maybe just send a photo of the cat. that is how we used to talk before everything got difficult. the cat is asleep on my shoes. i'll take the photo and see.
partner work
Two people are asked to work together.

we had to make a poster about rivers. i drew the river and she did the writing. mine looked like a road so i coloured it blue. still a road really. we didn't talk much. i was trying to think of something to say the whole time and then the lesson ended
again
Return to a place you used to know.
went past the old school. gate was shut. couldn't see my classroom because there's a new building in front of it. thought i'd feel something more than annoyed about the building but i didn't really.
one good thing
Something small improves a bad day.

the bus driver waited. i was running and i know he saw me ages before i got there because he was looking in the mirror. usually they pretend they cant see you. i said thank you too loudly and sat right at the front because my legs felt weird. then i realised i had the wrong ticket and he just waved me on. i nearly cried which is stupid, it's a bus ticket. had been a horrible day before that. i don't want to write all of it down. i just want to remember that someone waited when he didn't have to.
room 12
A hotel room contains someone else's belongings.

Room twelve was already occupied. Not by a person, by a suitcase. Open on the bed, half unpacked. Recpetion said there was no booking for it and I must have the wrong room. I held up the key. They gave me another room. At two in the morning someone tried my door. Same reception boy, carrying the suitcase. He said it was mine. I said it wasn't. He looked so tired I almost accepted it. In the morning it was outside my door with a note saying sorry for the inconvenience. I left it there. On the train I kept wondering whether I should have opened it, then remembered I had already seen inside. Shirts. A hairbrush. An orange peeled halfway.
junction
You have time to change your mind.

There were two trains and either would get me there. One went through the city where he lived. I'd checked this three times, although it wasn't relevant because I wasn't getting off. The other was faster and cost less. I bought the slower ticket. Then stood at the junction watching the faster train arrive first. I could still change it. The woman beside me was eating an apple very loudly and I started using her bites as a countdown, which makes no sense but I was tired. Three more bites and I'd move. She put the apple in her bag. My train came. I got on and took a seat facing backwards, so at least I wouldn't see the city coming.
Window
Describe a journey without the destination.

the window rattles when we go fast and stops when we slow down. fields then houses then fields again. somebody behind me is opening a packet very carefully and making it take longer. i have no signal. the reflection of my face floats over a horse.
the drawer
A house makes a new sound.

The drawer opened every time the extractor fan came on. At first I thought vibration. Then I put a heavy book in front of it and the drawer pushed the book off the counter. I had people coming for dinner and wasn't going to cancel because of a drawer. I taped it shut. Halfway through frying the onions the tape stretched, slowly, until there was a thin gap. Someone inside said could you keep it down. I said I'm cooking. They said yes, they could tell. I turned the fan off and opened the window instead. By dessert I'd almost forgotten. Then my friend went to find a spoon and I shouted at her so loudly she dropped the bowl.
boiling
A ghost joins an ordinary routine.

The kettle boiled without being plugged in. Useful, I thought. I know that's not the right response but electricity is expensive. After a week it started making two cups. I drank one and left the other.

By Friday there was toast. Buttered badly, right to the edges on one slice and none in the middle of the other. That's when I got upset. My father made toast like that. I sat down and said if it's you, I need you to do something else. Something definite. The kitchen went quiet. Then the radio came on to a station he hated, very loud, and I laughed and cried at the same time because that was also something he'd do by accident.
photo
An old photograph changes.

In the photograph my aunt is standing behind the chair. Yesterday she was sitting in it. I asked Mum and she said there were two photographs from that day. There aren't. I took the frame apart. One photo, cardboard, glass. When I put it back she was sitting again. I don't want to sound dramatic but I've put it face down. Mum turned it over while dusting. Now the chair is empty and my aunt is standing much nearer the camera.
the tap
Someone answers from an empty room.

'Can you turn the tap off?' I called from the hall. 'In a minute,' someone called back. I was alone. I knew I was alone because I'd spent all morning enjoying it. I stood with my coat half on, listening to the water run. It sounded like the upstairs basin. I said who is that, and the voice said in a minute again, impatient this time. I went outside and rang my sister. She told me not to go back in. Good advice, except my dog was still inside. Through the letterbox I could see him sitting at the bottom of the stairs, tail going. He never does that for strangers. I called his name and he looked at me like I was interrupting.
lead
A dog chooses the route.

Dog turned left so I turned left. Usually we go right. He dragged me past the park, past the bakery, straight into a car wash. No idea why. A man came out holding a hose and the dog went absolutely mad with happiness. Turns out the man used to own him. Not own him, foster him before us. I stood there feeling weirdly jealous while my dog tried to climb inside somebody else's coat. Then he came back and leaned on my leg, still watching the man.
hill
Keep moving even when you regret starting.

Halfway up I thought I'd be sick so I slowed down but Jess was behind me and I didn't want her to think I'd stopped. Stupid. She'd already seen me fall over a bin earlier. The hill kept bending and every bend looked like the top until you got there. My shirt was stuck to my back. I could hear my breath louder than the music. At the actual top there was no view, just a fence and somebody's shed. Jess arrived walking. Said she'd walked most of it. I sat on the gravel. She had brought sweets. We ate them without saying anything, then had to decide how to get down because my legs had started shaking.
over
A small jump goes wrong.
Jumped the puddle. Cleared the water. Landed in mud on the other side and slid straight back into it. Dog watched. Didn't even try to help. Whole left shoe full of water now.
race
Someone cheers for the wrong person.

The woman kept shouting go Danny and I kept running faster even though I'm not Danny. I was tired enough that encouragment was encouragement. She ran along the barrier beside me for a bit and then stopped. I looked over. Her face had changed. Actual Danny was behind me, limping, and I'd been soaking up his mother's support for the last hundred metres. I slowed down without meaning to. He caught me at the corner. We ran together for a bit. He said you can go ahead. I said I couldn't actually, I'd used everything trying to impress his mum. He laughed so hard he had to stop and now I felt responsible for that too.
the gap
An animal escapes through a small opening.

He got through a gap I couldn't even fit my hand into. One secod dog, next second tail, then nothing. I called and heard him crashing about behind the fence. We were beside the railway so so I went cold all over. Tried climbing, slipped, ripped my sleeve. A man in a van stopped and asked what I was doing. I said dog, just dog, couldn't make a sentence. He had bolt cutters. Why he had bolt cutters I didn't ask. We got a panel open and there was my idiot sitting beside a sandwich wrapper, eating bread. I grabbed his collar so hard he yelped. Then I sat down in the dirt holding him and couldn't get up for a minute.
